use: Data has a time axis; user needs to observe rise/fall trends or rate of change over a continuous period
not: Fewer than 4 data points (use stat card); more than 6 series (visual noise); no time dimension exists
volume: <1000 pts: SVG; ≥1000 pts: Canvas + downsampling; >10000: aggregate to intervals
colour: Primary: #0080FF. Multiple series: distinct colors + distinct line styles. Fill: 20% opacity
a11y: Use solid, dashed, and dotted line styles plus direct series labels; never distinguish series by hue alone.
fallback: Visible data table plus concise trend summary. Keyboard: focus reveals hover values; +/- buttons zoom; Reset restores the full range.

use: Comparing discrete categories by magnitude; ranking or ordering is the core insight; categories ≤ 15
not: Categories > 15 (use table or search); data has time dimension (use line); showing proportions (use waffle/stacked)
volume: <20 categories: vertical bar; 20–50: horizontal bar; >50: paginated table
colour: Each bar: distinct color. Grouped: same hue family. Always sort descending by value
a11y: Use direct category/value labels and group outlines or patterns; never encode category solely by bar color. Do not rely on color alone.
fallback: Visible sortable data table plus concise comparison summary. Keyboard: focus reveals hover values; focusable headers with Enter/Space sort and aria-sort reports direction.

use: ≤5 categories; one dominant segment vs rest; emphasis on visual proportion over exact values
not: Categories > 5; slice differences < 5% (visually indistinguishable); user needs precise values; accessibility-first context
volume: Max 6 slices; beyond that switch to stacked bar 100%
colour: 5–6 max colors. Contrasting palette. Largest slice at 12 o'clock. Always label slices with %
a11y: Pie charts do not inherently fail WCAG; unlabeled color-only slices are inaccessible. Use direct labels and patterns, with a non-pie fallback. Do not rely on color alone.
fallback: Percentage data table and concise part-to-whole summary; offer a stacked bar view. Keyboard: focus reveals slice values; Enter/Space drills in; Back button returns.

use: Exploring relationship between two continuous variables; identifying clusters or outliers in a dataset
not: Variables are categorical (use grouped bar); fewer than 20 points (patterns aren't meaningful); mobile-primary context
volume: <500 pts: SVG; 500–5000: Canvas at 0.6–0.8 opacity; >5000: hexbin or aggregate first
colour: Color axis: gradient (blue → red). Bubble size: relative to 3rd variable. Opacity: 0.6–0.8 to show density
a11y: Combine marker shapes with direct group labels; color may reinforce but must not be the only distinction.
fallback: Visible data table plus correlation summary. Keyboard: focus reveals point values; labeled start/end range inputs replace brush dragging.

use: Showing intensity/density across a 2D grid; time-based patterns (e.g., activity by hour × day)
not: Fewer than 20 cells (use bar); user needs to read exact values; colorblind users without pattern fallback
volume: Up to 10,000 cells efficiently; beyond that aggregate; calendar heatmap: 365 cells max per SVG
colour: Gradient: Cool (blue) to Hot (red). Divergent scale for ±data. Always include numeric color legend
a11y: Print values or symbols in cells and use texture/labels in addition to the color scale. Do not rely on color alone.
fallback: Grid data table plus intensity summary. Keyboard: focus reveals cell values; +/- buttons zoom; Reset restores the grid.

use: Data has a regional/location dimension; spatial distribution is the core insight for the user
not: Regions have very different sizes making visual comparison misleading (use bar); mobile-primary context
volume: <1000 regions: SVG; ≥1000: Canvas/WebGL (Deck.gl); global maps: tile-based rendering
colour: Single color gradient per region group. Categorized colors for discrete types. Legend with clear scale breaks
a11y: Label regions directly and pair fills with boundaries or patterns; location meaning cannot depend on color alone.
fallback: Sortable region table plus geographic summary. Keyboard: arrow keys or labeled pan buttons move the map; +/- buttons zoom; Enter drills into a focused region; Back returns.

use: Sequential multi-stage process; showing conversion or drop-off rates between defined stages
not: Stages aren't sequential; values don't decrease monotonically (use bar); fewer than 3 stages
volume: 3–8 stages optimal; beyond 8 stages group minor steps into 'Other'
colour: Stages: single color gradient (start → end). Show conversion % between each stage. Highlight biggest drop
a11y: Keep stage names and values visible and distinguish stages with text and boundaries, not only a gradient. Do not rely on color alone.
fallback: Linear stage table/list plus conversion summary. Keyboard: focus reveals stage values; Enter/Space drills in; Back returns.

use: Single KPI measured against a defined target or threshold; dashboard summary context
not: No target or benchmark exists; comparing multiple KPIs at once (use bullet chart grid)
volume: Single metric per gauge; for 3+ KPIs use bullet chart grid layout
colour: Performance: Red → Yellow → Green gradient. Target: marker line. Threshold zones clearly differentiated
a11y: Place the number and target text beside the gauge and label threshold zones; red/yellow/green alone is insufficient.
fallback: Visible KPI/target text and a one-row data table plus status summary. Keyboard: focus reveals the same detail as hover.

use: Historical data + model predictions; communicating uncertainty range to non-technical stakeholders
not: No historical baseline; prediction confidence is too low to be useful; audience is not data-literate
volume: Keep historical window to 30–90 days for readability; forecast horizon ≤ 30% of visible x-axis range
colour: Actual: solid line #0080FF. Forecast: dashed #FF9500. Confidence band: 15% opacity fill same hue
a11y: Use solid actual and dashed forecast lines, direct labels, and a named confidence range; hue alone is insufficient.
fallback: Visible forecast table plus uncertainty summary. Keyboard: focus reveals hover values; buttons toggle actual/forecast; +/- buttons zoom; Reset restores range.

use: Monitoring a time-series for outliers; alerting users to unexpected spikes or dips in operational data
not: Anomalies are predefined categories (use bar with highlight); real-time context without a pause control
volume: Stream at ≤60fps with Canvas; batch: up to 10,000 pts; mark anomalies as a separate data layer
colour: Normal: #0080FF solid line. Anomaly marker: #FF0000 circle + filled. Alert band: #FFF3CD background zone
a11y: Mark anomalies with a distinct shape and text annotation as well as color. Do not rely on color alone.
fallback: Anomaly event list/table plus narrative alert summary. Keyboard: focus reveals point details; alerts are available in the persistent list without hover.

use: Showing size relationships within a hierarchy; overview of proportional structure (e.g., budget breakdown)
not: Hierarchy depth > 3 levels (too complex to read); user needs to compare sibling values precisely
volume: <200 nodes: SVG; 200–1000: Canvas; >1000: paginate or pre-filter before rendering
colour: Parent nodes: distinct hues. Children: lighter shades of same hue. White separator borders: 2–3px
a11y: Label hierarchy nodes and use borders/patterns as well as hue; make the tree table the primary accessible view. Do not rely on color alone.
fallback: Collapsible tree table plus hierarchy summary; treemap remains supplementary. Keyboard: focus reveals hover values; Enter/Space drills or expands; Back collapses/returns.

use: Showing how quantities flow between nodes; multi-source multi-target distribution
not: Flow directions form loops (use network graph); fewer than 3 source-target pairs; mobile-primary context
volume: <50 flows: SVG; ≥50: Canvas; >200 flows: aggregate minor flows into 'Other' node
colour: Gradient from source to target color. Flow opacity: 0.4–0.6. Node labels always visible
a11y: Label source, target, and value; use line style or node symbols in addition to gradient color. Do not rely on color alone.
fallback: Source-to-target flow table plus flow summary. Keyboard: focus reveals hover values; Enter/Space drills into a node; Back returns.

use: Showing how individual positive/negative components add up to a final total (e.g., P&L, budget variance)
not: Changes are not additive; more than 12 bars (readability breaks); audience expects a simple total
volume: 4–12 bars optimal; beyond 12 aggregate minor items into a single 'Other' bar
colour: Increases: #4CAF50. Decreases: #F44336. Start total: #2196F3. End total: #0D47A1. Running total line: dashed
a11y: Pair increase/decrease bars with signed values and directional icons, not red/green alone. Do not rely on color alone.
fallback: Running-total table plus variance summary. Keyboard: focus reveals the same value as hover.

use: Comparing multiple entities across the same fixed set of attributes (e.g., product feature comparison)
not: Axes > 8 (unreadable); values need precise comparison (use grouped bar); audience unfamiliar with radar charts
volume: 2–3 datasets maximum per chart; 5–8 axes; beyond 8 axes switch to parallel coordinates
colour: Single dataset: #0080FF at 20% fill. Multiple: distinct hues with 30% fill. Border: full opacity
a11y: Use line styles, point shapes, and direct series labels in addition to color. Do not rely on color alone.
fallback: Raw data table and grouped-bar alternative plus comparison summary. Keyboard: focus reveals values; buttons toggle series.

use: Financial time-series with Open/High/Low/Close data; trading or investment product context only
not: Non-financial audience; no OHLC data available (use line chart); accessibility-first context
volume: Real-time: Canvas required. Historical: paginate by time range. Max 500 candles visible at once
colour: Bullish: #26A69A. Bearish: #EF5350. Volume bars: 40% opacity below. Body fill vs hollow for OHLC style
a11y: Use filled versus hollow candles and OHLC text values; bullish/bearish meaning cannot depend on color. Do not rely on color alone.
fallback: Sortable OHLC table plus daily-change summary. Keyboard: focus reveals candle values; +/- buttons zoom; Reset restores range; live updates do not steal focus.

use: Mapping connections between entities; network topology or social graph exploration context
not: Node count > 500 without clustering pre-applied; user needs precise connection counts; mobile context
volume: ≤100 nodes: SVG; 101–500: Canvas; >500: must apply clustering/LOD before rendering
colour: Node types: categorical colors. Edges: #90A4AE at 60% opacity. Highlight path: #F59E0B
a11y: Use labeled node types, shapes, and edge styles in addition to color; the adjacency view is the accessible source of truth. Do not rely on color alone.
fallback: Adjacency list/table and relationship summary; tree view when applicable. Keyboard: focus reveals node details; Enter drills; Move up/down/left/right buttons replace drag.

use: Showing spread, median, and outliers of a dataset; comparing distributions across multiple groups
not: Fewer than 20 data points per group (distribution is not meaningful); audience unfamiliar with statistical charts
volume: Any sample size; aggregated representation so rendering is ⚡ Excellent at any volume
colour: Box fill: #BBDEFB. Border: #1976D2. Median line: #D32F2F bold. Outlier dots: #F44336
a11y: Label median, quartiles, whiskers, and outliers directly; do not use color alone for statistical roles.
fallback: Statistics table plus distribution summary. Keyboard: focus reveals the same statistics as hover.

use: Dashboard with multiple KPIs side by side; space-constrained contexts where a gauge is too large
not: Single KPI with emphasis (use gauge); data has no defined target range; fewer than 3 KPIs
volume: Ideal for 3–10 bullet charts in a grid; scales to any count efficiently
colour: Qualitative ranges: #FFCDD2 / #FFF9C4 / #C8E6C9 (bad/ok/good). Performance bar: #1976D2. Target: black 3px marker
a11y: Label every qualitative range and target with text; color is supplementary.
fallback: Visible KPI/target table plus status summary. Keyboard: focus reveals the same detail as hover.

use: Showing what fraction of a whole is filled; percentage progress in a visually engaging and accessible format
not: More than 5 categories (use stacked bar); exact values matter over visual proportion; very tight space
volume: 10×10 grid standard (100 cells); for > 5 categories switch to stacked 100% bar
colour: 3–5 categories max. 2–3px gap between cells. Each category a distinct accessible color pair
a11y: Label each category and percentage and add patterns or symbols; filled-cell color alone is insufficient.
fallback: Percentage table/list plus part-to-whole summary. Keyboard: focus reveals each cell value.

use: Exploring nested proportions where both hierarchy and relative size matter (e.g., org spend breakdown)
not: More than 3 hierarchy levels (outer rings become unreadable); precision matters over overview; mobile
volume: <100 nodes: SVG; 100–500: Canvas; >500: filter to top N before rendering
colour: Center to outer: darker to lighter hue. Each level 15–20% lighter. Contrasting border between sectors
a11y: Label hierarchy levels and segments and use boundaries/patterns as well as hue; the indented list is primary. Do not rely on color alone.
fallback: Collapsible indented list/table plus hierarchy summary and breadcrumbs. Keyboard: Enter/Space drills or expands; Back button returns; focus reveals hover detail.

use: Decomposing a metric into contributing factors; AI-assisted analysis or BI drill-down scenarios
not: No clear parent-child causal relationship; audience expects a summary rather than exploration
volume: Up to 5 levels deep; limit visible nodes to 20 per level for readability; lazy-load deeper levels
colour: Positive impact nodes: #2563EB. Negative impact nodes: #EF4444. Neutral connectors: #94A3B8
a11y: Name each node and contribution and use shapes/connector styles in addition to color. Do not rely on color alone.
fallback: Expandable tree table plus root-cause summary. Keyboard: Enter/Space drills and expands; Back collapses; dedicated expand/collapse buttons expose the same operations.

use: Scientific/engineering context where Z-axis carries essential info not expressible in 2D
not: 2D projection conveys the same insight; mobile context; accessibility-required environments; standard business dashboards
volume: WebGL required. Deck.gl: up to 1M points. Three.js: LOD required beyond 50,000 pts
colour: Depth cues: lighting and shading. Z-axis: color gradient (cool → warm). Transparent overlapping: opacity 0.4
a11y: Use labels, shapes, and depth-independent cues; color and 3D position cannot be the only carriers of meaning.
fallback: Mandatory 2D projection, data table, and spatial summary. Keyboard: rotate/pan buttons and +/- zoom controls replace pointer/VR manipulation; Reset returns the camera.

use: Live monitoring dashboards; IoT/ops data updating at ≥1 Hz; user needs current value at a glance
not: Update frequency < 1/min (use periodic-refresh line chart); flashing content without reduced-motion support
volume: Canvas/WebGL required. Buffer last 60–300s of data. Downsample older data on scroll
colour: Current pulse: #00FF00 (dark theme) or #0080FF (light theme). History: fading opacity. Grid: dark background
a11y: Show the current value and status text and use line styles or markers in addition to color. Do not rely on color alone.
fallback: Streaming data table plus current-value/trend summary. Keyboard: Pause/Resume button controls updates; focus reveals values; +/- buttons zoom; Reset restores range.

use: NLP output visualization; exploratory analysis of text corpus sentiment; frequency-weighted keyword overview
not: Precise values matter (word size is inherently imprecise); screen-reader context; corpus < 50 items
volume: 50–5000 terms optimal. Beyond 5000: apply top-N filtering before render. Avoid on mobile
colour: Positive: #22C55E. Negative: #EF4444. Neutral: #94A3B8. Word size maps to frequency
a11y: Expose every term, count, and sentiment as text; size and color are supplementary only.
fallback: Sortable term table/list plus sentiment summary; word cloud is supplementary. Keyboard: focus reveals word details; labeled controls filter with Space/Enter.

use: Analyzing event logs to visualize actual process flows; identifying bottlenecks and deviations in ops/product funnels
not: No event log data available; audience expects a static flowchart (use diagram tool); node count > 100 without pre-filtering
volume: <30 nodes: SVG; 30–100: Canvas; >100: apply variant filtering (top 80% of cases) before rendering
colour: Happy path: #10B981 thick line. Deviations: #F59E0B thin line. Bottleneck nodes: #EF4444 fill
a11y: Label nodes and paths and use shapes/line styles in addition to color; bottlenecks require text annotations. Do not rely on color alone.
fallback: Path summary table plus bottleneck narrative. Keyboard: Move buttons replace drag; focus reveals node details; Enter activates a node; Back returns.
